description: Canonical, declarative inventory of Cursor-Governance Python test-suite topology. This is NOT a second version authority: exact dependency versions live in pyproject.toml and are mirrored in requirements.txt. This file declares only which suites exist, how they are isolated, and which false-positive test-shaped paths are intentionally excluded. Consumed by ops/scripts/run_python_test_suites.py (executor) and ops/scripts/validate_python_contract.py (fail-closed drift validator).

local_pr_check.note: make pr passes --changed-file to the runner. make test, make pr-full, and CI keep the catalog including repo-root '.'.

substitutions.PYTHON: absolute path of the current Python interpreter (sys.executable)

suites.rationale: Root discovery over the whole repository with root autonomy/ on PYTHONPATH. Explicitly ignores the three separately-owned active suites (each has its own registry entry) so it neither shadows their packages nor double-runs them. Non-test false positives are ignored via pyproject addopts. CI profile keeps root-only coverage XML + terminal coverage, xdist, the 300s per-test timeout, and the existing zero-percent advisory threshold. Local make pr must not pass this suite's '.' collection root; it uses --changed-file and select_pr_pytest_paths.py instead.

Skill-local executable evidence is a first-class suite rather than an incidental pytest side effect. The canonical Python contract remains the registry: skill_self_test_roots declares which live skill packs own self-tests, while run_skill_self_tests.py discovers every skills/*/scripts/*self_test.py, fails closed when a new test appears under an unregistered skill root, and executes each discovered script in a fresh Python process from its own skill root. Owning skills/ ensures a changed or newly-added skill self-test selects this suite before it can become invisible.

Root autonomy/ (W7 control plane) and environment/program-execution/peer_execution/autonomy/ (Claude Code bounded-concurrency runtime) share the top-level package name, so this suite runs with cwd and PYTHONPATH=environment/program-execution/peer_execution to bind the correct package. '-o addopts=' clears root pytest settings so the root active-suite ignores cannot reintroduce package shadowing here. CI profile keeps xdist and the 300s timeout with no root coverage arguments. peer_execution/autonomy is also ignored by repo-root to avoid double collection.

The Wave 3 generated-data suite is globally ignored by root pytest and driven by its own unittest orchestrator (run_wave3_tests.py), which shells out to `python -m unittest discover` over the conformance/routing/negative/golden directories. Run as an opaque command in both profiles: no pytest arguments are appended and any nonzero result fails the whole runner.

Program Execution controller validation. Its VALIDATION.md states fresh-process isolation is intentional because several fixtures create and intentionally abandon or fail Git worktrees; therefore this suite is a command_sequence run in fresh processes and is NOT collected by root pytest or run through xdist. The three commands run sequentially from the controller-template directory; execution stops on the first failed command and preserves its exact exit status. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 is required because validate_controller.py rejects any __pycache__/.pyc under the template as 'compiled Python debris'; without it the per-file test step would leave bytecode that the negative-test step's controller validation then fails on (matches the subsystem's own PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 Makefile convention). The middle command runs one fresh process per test file concurrently rather than `unittest discover` in a single process: VALIDATION.md prescribes exactly that per-file isolation (fixtures abandon or fail Git worktrees), and discover was both slower (96s -> 27s measured on 4 cores) and weaker isolation than the documented matrix. The same 105 tests run either way; xargs exits non-zero if any file fails. Concurrency is $PES_CONTROLLER_JOBS, else the online CPU count.
